notes: Lorain County BOE's actual site is voteloraincountyohio.gov (loraincountyelections.gov does not resolve). Sources: certified General Candidate List (dated 09/14/2026), certified 2026 General Issues List (9/9/2026), the Ballot Text PDF (scanned; English text recovered by OCR, so a few digits/words were cleaned up where the scan was unreadable), and the 46-Day FWAB issues notice (9/18/2026) for precinct coverage. Only three county-run candidate contests are on this county's Nov 3, 2026 ballot (Probate judge, County Commissioner, County Auditor); no municipal, township or school-board candidate races. County Commissioner also has a certified write-in candidate, Andrew Lipian, who does not appear on the ballot and is therefore not listed. Probate judge is nonpartisan on the ballot (board lists no party). State Issue 3 excluded. Issue scopes: Issue 5 (Erie County General Health District, Erie County controlling) is voted only in Vermilion City precincts 1A, 3A/5A, 4A, 5B, so it is filed as scope city/Vermilion. Issue 6 (Herrick Memorial Library) is a library district covering all of Wellington Township and Village, all of Brighton Township, all of Huntington Township, and parts of Pittsfield and Rochester townships/village; filed as scope township/Wellington because the schema has no library-district scope. Issue 7 (Lorain County General Health District renewal) is countywide except Vermilion City; filed as scope county. Issue 10 (Strongsville City SD, Cuyahoga controlling) votes only in parts of Columbia Township precincts 2 and 5. Issue 11 (Vermilion Local SD, Erie controlling) votes in Vermilion City, part of Brownhelm Township and part of Lorain City 8A. Issue 1 (Amherst EVSD) covers Amherst City, Amherst Township and parts of Lorain City; Issue 2 (Clearview LSD) covers Lorain City 4E, part of 5A/5C/6C and Sheffield Township; Issue 4 (Elyria CSD) covers most of Elyria City, Elyria Township and parts of Amherst/Carlisle townships and Lorain 4F; Issues 8-9 (Oberlin CSD) cover Oberlin City and parts of Amherst, Carlisle, New Russia and Pittsfield townships. Issue numbers are not sequential on the board's list (36 and 35 were added late); numbering kept as the board prints it.

issues.name: Issue 18 — Village of Grafton charter amendment (Article V, Sections 1 and 2 — appointment of Clerk of Council and Director of Finance)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall Article V, 1 and 2 of the Charter of Village of Grafton be amended as follows: Granting Council the authority to appoint a Clerk of Council and the Mayor to appoint a qualified Director of Finance. (Full text: effective January 1, 2028, Council may appoint a Clerk of Council serving at its pleasure; the Mayor shall appoint a Director of Finance, confirmed by Council, who must hold an accredited finance degree or five years' professional finance experience and who keeps the municipality's financial records and custody of public money.) YES / NO

(Full text establishes the positions of Law Director, Police Chief, Fire Chief, Building Inspector, Village Administrator and Village Engineer; Police Chief, Fire Chief and Village Engineer must meet Ohio Revised Code sections 109.804, 737.22 and 4733.01; Council may create, combine or abolish departments by ordinance.) YES / NO

issues.name: Issue 20 — Village of Grafton charter amendment (Article XIV — Charter Review Commission)
issues.ballotLanguage: Shall Article XIV of the Charter of Village of Grafton be amended as follows: Starting in 2026, every 3 years Council shall appoint an unpaid, 5-member Charter Review Commission to recommend charter changes. (Full text: commencing in 2026 and each three years thereafter, Council appoints five electors holding no elective office to review the Charter and recommend changes within sixty days; Council submits any proposed changes to the electors no later than the next general election; meetings are public.) YES / NO
